edges.description: The displaced lens produces refractive error that, in children, converts to axial myopia through the defocus it introduces.
Lens tilt and decentration produce irregular astigmatism.
An anteriorly displaced lens can block the pupil and close the angle, producing secondary glaucoma.
Retinal detachment is a sight-threatening complication of ectopia lentis, frequent after lens removal in at least one FBN1 pedigree.

edges.description: Reproduces the zonular lesion and the resulting lens dislocation by removing fibrillin-1 from the cells that make the zonule.
edges.limitations: The model removes fibrillin-1 rather than carrying a heterozygous cysteine-missense or in-frame splice allele, so it shows that zonular fibrillin-1 is required, not how the dominant human alleles act. The deletion is confined to the eye by design, so it cannot address why the human alleles spare the aorta.

nodes.description: Fibrillin-1 microfibrils are the structural element of the zonular fibres (suspensory ligament of the lens). Defective microfibril assembly leaves the zonule stretched, weak or disrupted, so it no longer holds the lens centred behind the iris. In this disorder the defect is clinically confined to the eye: the aortic wall and skeleton are spared, a tissue restriction for which no mechanism has been established.

evidence.snippet: Congenital ectopia lentis (EL) refers to the congenital dysplasia or weakness of the lens suspensory ligament, resulting in an abnormal position of the crystalline lens

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deletion of fibrillin-1 in the mouse eye results in ectopia lentis and other ocular phenotypes associated with Marfan syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Conditional knockout of Fbn1 in NPCE, but not lens, profoundly affected the ciliary zonule, the system of fibrillin-rich fibers that centers the lens in the eye.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deletion of fibrillin-1 in the mouse eye results in ectopia lentis and other ocular phenotypes associated with Marfan syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The tensile strength of the fibrillin-depleted zonule was reduced substantially, due to a shift toward production of smaller caliber fibers.

evidence.reference_title: Development, composition, and structural arrangements of the ciliary zonule of the mouse.
evidence.snippet: Fbn2 expression by nonpigmented ciliary epithelial cells diminished postnatally and there was a concomitant increase in Fbn1 expression, especially in cells located in valleys between the ciliary folds.

nodes.description: Displacement of the crystalline lens, typically bilateral. The defining feature of the disorder. Age at recognition varies widely: a median of three years in one Chinese series and 35 years in a British series of FBN1 carriers, and late-onset dislocation is also reported.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype variant screening and phenotypic analysis of FBN1 in Chinese patients with isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: Systemic clinical examination of the twelve probands indicated that all had bilateral EL with a median age at diagnosis of three years.

evidence.reference_title: A genotype-phenotype comparison of ADAMTSL4 and FBN1 in isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: Median age of diagnosis of EL was 35 years in patients with FBN1 mutations and 2 years in patients with ADAMTSL4 mutations (P < 0.01).

evidence.reference_title: Late-onset bilateral lens dislocation and glaucoma associated with a novel mutation in FBN1.
evidence.snippet: four members in three generations were affected by late-onset lens dislocation and secondary glaucoma but had no signs of cardiovascular abnormality or abnormal skeletal features

evidence.reference_title: Role of ADAMTSL4 mutations in FBN1 mutation-negative ectopia lentis patients.
evidence.snippet: Causative FBN1 mutations were identified in 23/36 (64%) of probands while homozygous or compound heterozygous ADAMTSL4 mutations were identified in 6/12 (50%) of the remaining probands.

evidence.reference_title: Role of ADAMTSL4 mutations in FBN1 mutation-negative ectopia lentis patients.
evidence.snippet: The dominant disorder can be caused by mutations in FBN1, at the milder end of the type-1 fibrillinopathies spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent FBN1 mutation (R62C) in a Chinese family with isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: A recurrent mutation of FBN1 gene resulted in an arginine-to-cysteine residue (p.R62C), is responsible for the patients with isolated ectopia lentis in a Chinese family.

evidence.reference_title: A novel FBN1 mutation in a Chinese family with isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: A novel mutation of FBN1 results in an arginine to cysteine residue (p.R974C) substitution, which is responsible for the patients with isolated EL in this Chinese family.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype variant screening and phenotypic analysis of FBN1 in Chinese patients with isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: The seven pathogenic variants were identified in 8/12 (66.7%) probands with IEL.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of Novel and Recurrent FBN1 Gene Mutations in Two Unrelated Turkish Families with Isolated Ectopia Lentis: A Case Report with Insights from a Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: Segregation analysis demonstrated that both variants co-segregated with the ectopia lentis phenotype and were completely absent in unaffected family members as well as in WES data from 200 ophthalmologically normal in-house controls.

nodes.description: Fbn1 was deleted from either the lens or the non-pigmented ciliary epithelium. Only the ciliary-epithelium deletion affected the zonule: its fibres were thinner and weaker, ruptured by 3 months, and the mice developed ectopia lentis, later followed by cataract and enlarged eyes.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline FBN1 variant, most often a missense change that introduces or removes a cysteine in a calcium-binding EGF-like or TB domain, or a splice variant that skips an exon in frame. Variants in exons 24-32 are under-represented and premature-truncation variants have not been reported, which distinguishes the allelic spectrum from classical Marfan syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic FBN1 mutations in 146 adults not meeting clinical diagnostic criteria for Marfan syndrome: further delineation of type 1 fibrillinopathies and focus on patients with an isolated major criterion.
evidence.snippet: In patients with isolated EL, missense mutations involving a cysteine were predominant, mutations in exons 24-32 were underrepresented, and no mutations leading to a premature truncation were found.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of Novel and Recurrent FBN1 Gene Mutations in Two Unrelated Turkish Families with Isolated Ectopia Lentis: A Case Report with Insights from a Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: our study focused review of the literature on FBN1-associated IEL revealed that approximately 66.7% of reported variants involve missense substitutions affecting cysteine residues

evidence.reference_title: Novel FBN1 intron variant causes isolated ectopia lentis via in-frame exon skipping.
evidence.snippet: The causality of the variant in the skipping of exon 11, which results in an in-frame deletion of 60 amino acids corresponding to the "hinge" region of FBN1 protein, was confirmed in a minigene experiment.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous; predominantly cysteine-involving missense, with in-frame exon-skipping splice variants also reported.

nodes.description: Secondary glaucoma, including pupillary-block angle-closure glaucoma, occurs in FBN1-related isolated ectopia lentis and can be the presenting problem in late-onset families. Different glaucoma types have been described within one family.

evidence.reference_title: Late-onset bilateral lens dislocation and glaucoma associated with a novel mutation in FBN1.
evidence.snippet: Late-onset isolated ectopia lentis with secondary glaucoma is consistent with a novel mutation in FBN1.

evidence.reference_title: Ophthalmic findings in a family with early-onset isolated ectopia lentis and the p.Arg62Cys mutation of the fibrillin-1 gene (FBN1).
evidence.snippet: Our study presented detailed clinical manifestations, including some novel ophthalmic findings, such as pupillary abnormality, different types of glaucoma, and progressive hyperopia.

nodes.description: High myopia was the commonest associated finding in an isolated ectopia lentis series. FBN1 carriers in a British series had a normal mean axial length (22.74 mm), unlike ADAMTSL4 carriers, so the myopia is at least partly lenticular rather than axial.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype variant screening and phenotypic analysis of FBN1 in Chinese patients with isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: High myopia was the most common feature among the probands (83.3%; 10/12 cases).

evidence.reference_title: A genotype-phenotype comparison of ADAMTSL4 and FBN1 in isolated ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: Mean axial length was 22.74 mm (95% confidence interval [CI]: 21.3-24.2) (FBN1) and 27.54 mm (95% CI: 24.2-30.9) (ADAMTSL4) (P < 0.01).

nodes.description: Removal of the dislocated lens by pars plana vitreolensectomy, followed by optical rehabilitation of the aphakic eye. In one FBN1 pedigree, secondary iris-claw intraocular lenses gave better visual outcomes than aphakic contact lenses.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of non-syndromic ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: In this cohort, refractive management with iris-claw IOLs provided superior outcomes to contact lenses and the authors recommend this as the optimal refractive correction in EL patients.

nodes.description: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, often bilateral and frequently after vitreolensectomy, was present in every adult of one FBN1 pedigree with non-syndromic ectopia lentis.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of non-syndromic ectopia lentis.
evidence.snippet: Macula-on RRD was present in all individuals >18y, 64% (7/11 eyes) presenting post-vitreolensectomy with 57% having bilateral non-synchronous RRD.
